source: UK Summary Business Case (Five Case Model) - Padeswood CCUS Project

risks.description: Revenue Support Agreement (RSA) risk. RSA would be paid to the T&S Company (Eni) in two circumstances: where the network is underutilised, and where users are unavailable to inject CO2 and therefore are not paying user fees. [Financial Case Sec 5.4.1, p.14-15.]
risks.mitigation: Padeswood joining the T&S network will reduce the level of network underutilisation and will therefore reduce RSA payments to the T&SCo.

risks.description: Discontinuation risk for Padeswood: the potential for Padeswood to be unable to continue under the business model contract due to the actions of another party or events outside its control - a large-scale, programme-wide issue (e.g. leakage), a prolonged T&S issue, or external events such as Qualifying Change in Law (QCiL), Qualifying Shutdown Events, or Force Majeure. Projects connected via a spurline can also be exposed to an additional risk if the spurline FID is taken after T&S FID, which is not within the capture project's control. [Financial Case Sec 5.4.2, p.14-15.]
risks.mitigation: The risk of having to make a discontinuation payment to Padeswood is judged to be a remote contingent liability given that it is very unlikely (<1%); spurline-timing risk is treated as a variation of the existing cross-chain risks already protected by the business model.

risks.description: Exchequer funding / Secretary of State direct agreement (SoSDA) risk: LCCC is only liable to make payments to the extent it has received sufficient funds from HMG, creating a risk that Padeswood would have no recourse under its private-law contract with LCCC to obtain payments owed if HMG funding to LCCC were insufficient. [Financial Case Sec 5.4.3, p.14-15.]
risks.mitigation: The Secretary of State will sign a direct agreement with Padeswood (to which LCCC is also party) to fund payments directly where LCCC fails to pay; this does not increase DESNZ's overall liabilities or create a contingent liability, as it is an intragroup transaction.

risks.description: Fraud risk across the CCUS programme's grant and contract payments. [Financial Case Sec 5.4.4, p.14-15.]
risks.mitigation: A CCUS Fraud Management Strategy is being developed specifying the programme's strategic approach to deterrence, prevention, detection, and management of fraud and error, including counter-fraud governance and reporting structures and high-quality fraud risk assessments (FRAs) for the different tranches of the CCUS programme.

risks.description: Financial sensitivities: several contractual terms are 'locked in' at Padeswood FID, but drivers of the financial impact continue to move post-FID - notably the carbon market price (Low ETS series used as the reference price for the extension period) and the opex reopener (higher opex expenditure payments), both of which could result in higher subsidy. Other financial sensitivities have the effect of reducing total subsidy. [Financial Case Sec 5.4.5, p.14-15.]
risks.mitigation: Sensitivity analysis has been conducted to estimate the scale of potential subsidy increase from each driver; offsetting sensitivities are also identified and tracked.

risks.description: Cross-chain and cross-cutting risks. Cross-chain risks are risks the private sector is exposed to through the network but cannot mitigate against - T&S Construction delay, Padeswood Construction Delay, Padeswood Underperformance, T&S Underperformance, and Discontinuation Provisions; Padeswood joining the HyNet cluster increases HMG's exposure to compensation payments should the T&S network fail or become unavailable. Cross-cutting risks - inflation risk, carbon price risk, and OpEx risk - are those which are challenging for the private sector to price or relate to events outside their control. [Financial Case Sec 5.4.6, p.14-15; overlaps in subject matter with the Economic Case's Sec 3.4 Risk Appraisal tables, p.10-11, which quantify the value-for-money impact of the same named risks but are a modelling input rather than a risk-register entry, and are excised from planning text for leakage safety but not scored here.]
risks.mitigation: Risk allocation is designed so that each risk sits with the party best placed to manage it; the business model contracts and Network Code are structured to limit and price cross-chain exposure.

notes:
STATUS: page-verified 2026-07-19 directly against the real downloaded PDF (data/raw/P-UK-PadeswoodCCUS/padeswood-summary-business-case.pdf, 17 pages, PyMuPDF direct read) - this is a first-pass extraction, not yet independently second-rated.

STRUCTURE: like HyNet, this UK Summary Business Case scatters risk content across two incompatible framings rather than one WB-style SORT table + Key Risks narrative: (1) Economic Case Sec 3.4 'Risk Appraisal' (p.10-11) - Table 4 (Cross Chain Risk Appraisal: T&S Construction Delay, User Construction Delay, User Underperformance, T&S Availability, Discontinuation) and Table 5 (Cross Cutting Risk Appraisal: Inflation, Commodity Price, Traded Carbon Price, Capex Overrun, Opex Overrun), each with only a one-line qualitative 'Net Impact on Value for Money' label (Negative/Neutral/n/a) and NO paired mitigation text - a value-for-money sensitivity table, not a risk register; (2) Financial Case Sec 5.4 'Financial Risks' (p.14-15) - six named, numbered risk items (5.4.1-5.4.6) each with prose description and identifiable mitigating mechanisms (contractual, governance, or assurance-based).

METHODOLOGY (same rule as HyNet, 2026-07-19): ground truth = ONE section per document. Chose Sec 5.4 over Sec 3.4 specifically because Sec 3.4's table has no mitigation field at all (would require fabricating mitigation text to fit the schema, which is not permitted), whereas Sec 5.4 pairs each named risk with real mitigating actions - closer structurally to a WB Key-Risks-narrative entry. Sec 3.4 is still excised from planning text for leakage safety (a model should not see pre-digested risk content in any framing) but is not scored against; R06's note above flags the explicit subject-matter overlap between the two sections (Discontinuation and the cross-chain/cross-cutting risk categories appear in both).

CAVEAT (flagged for a second rater): mitigation text for R01, R03, R05, and R06 is thinner and more implicit than the WB PAD baseline - the source describes payment/liability mechanisms and risk-allocation design rather than always using explicit 'this will be mitigated by...' framing. The mitigation fields here are a faithful paraphrase of the closest available text, not fabricated, but this document is structurally less mitigation-rich than the WB corpus and that should be considered when interpreting any recall/precision comparison against it.

EXCISION JUDGMENT CALL (flagged): page 12 (Commercial Case Sec 4.3-4.4) contains generic, non-itemized mentions of 'mitigate key investment risks' and 'cross-chain risks' plus boilerplate contract-clause language ('change in law and force majeure') that echoes Discontinuation's cause list (Sec 5.4.2) without naming it or restating its rating. Judged incidental (matches the precedent used for similar generic mentions elsewhere in the WB corpus, e.g. P-BFA/P-JOR/P-MAR/P-UGA rows in corpus_manifest.csv) and left in planning text rather than excised; page 12 is NOT in the excision range below.

EXCISION: proposed_excision_pages = '10-11, 14-15' (Sec 3.4 Risk Appraisal + Sec 5.4 Financial Risks); Sec 6.6 'Risk management' (p.17) is pure process/governance description (RAID, DESNZ risk guidance, escalation processes) with no named or rated risk items and is left as planning text, matching the same precedent applied to HyNet's Sec 6.7.
